Based on my chemistry knowledge, I can answer this question without further tool use.

When cyanides (like sodium cyanide or potassium cyanide) are mixed with organic acids (or any acids), they react to form hydrogen cyanide (HCN), which is a highly toxic gas. The reaction follows this general pattern:

NaCN + H⁺ → HCN + Na⁺

The hydrogen cyanide gas that forms is extremely toxic even in small amounts and can be rapidly fatal if inhaled. This is why mixing cyanide salts with acids is extremely dangerous in laboratory and industrial settings.
